title: GOES-16 and GOES-18 share 20 to 120 second changes but no narrow peak passes a fitted-noise test on 14 May 2024
abstract: We test rapid changes during the 14 May 2024 solar flare with independent GOES-16 and GOES-18 X-ray sensors. In 16:48 to 17:08 UTC, band-limited log-flux changes have correlations of 0.923 in XRS-B and 0.823 in XRS-A. Phase controls give conditional p-values of 0.0005. The largest 20 to 120 second spectral peaks give search-wide p-values of 0.104 to 0.512 against a fitted power law plus white noise. Four half-window XRS-B tests also remain above 0.05. Both spacecraft use fixed high-flux detectors in the main window. The result supports shared rapid variation, but does not resolve a narrow oscillation under this model. A changing flare, imperfect noise models, common processing, and particle contamination limit physical claims. No new source, planet, or physical mode is established. Code, input hashes, aggregate spectra, a figure, and retrieval steps are included. Raw external data remain outside the signed package.

display.caption: Two spacecraft measure shared rapid changes. Black curves show fitted noise spectra. Coherence and filtered changes are descriptive checks; they do not prove a physical oscillation.
